# `func T.m()` makes m a member of T, not a name of its own. The member list
# lives on T's declaration, so a method declared in one package is reachable
# through the type in another, and a second declaration of that member is a
# duplicate no matter which package each was written in.

# A method declared alongside its type is reachable through an import.
sngl test .
stdout 'ok'

# Redeclaring a member of an imported type is a duplicate, not a shadow.
cp dup.sngl.txt main.sngl
! sngl check .
stderr 'duplicate declaration of "shifted" on type Point'

-- main.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"
import d "./geom"
import app "sngl:app"

component main ui {
    var p d.Point = d.Point{x = 1}
    text #out(value=string(p.shifted()))
}

func testCrossPackageMethod(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.out.value == "2")
}

app.window {
    main
}
-- geom/geom.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import app "sngl:app"

struct Point {
    x int = 0
}

func Point.shifted(p Point) => p.x + 1

app.window {
}
-- dup.sngl.txt --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "./geom"

func Point.shifted(p Point) => p.x + 99

component main {
    text(value="x")
}
